docs.title: EasyShapes is a scientific software for constructing and simulating molecular systems.
docs.text:
Here is a brief overview of the main documentation sections:

  • Introduction – Provides a description of EasyShapes, including its purpose, licensing, latest release details, and contact information.
  • Installation & Setup – Guides users through system requirements, environment configuration, and the installation process.
  • User Guide – Covers core concepts, key terminology, workflow steps, and essential parameters for effective use of EasyShapes.
  • Tutorials – Offers practical, step-by-step examples demonstrating common workflows and data analysis tasks.

docs.title: Installation & Setup
docs.text:
EasyShapes is a cross-platform desktop application for Windows, macOS, and Linux, compatible with Python 3.11 through 3.13.

To install and set up EasyShapes, we recommend using Pixi, a modern package manager for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Main benefits of using Pixi
  • Ease of use: Pixi simplifies the installation process, making it accessible even for users with limited experience in package management.
  • Python version control: Pixi allows specifying and managing different Python versions for each project, ensuring compatibility.
  • Isolated environments: Pixi creates isolated environments for each project, preventing conflicts between different package versions.
  • PyPI and Conda support: Pixi can install packages from both PyPI and Conda repositories, providing access to a wide range of libraries.

A packaged application, which needs no Pixi, will be available on the GitHub Releases page later.

docs.title: Installing with Pixi recommended
docs.text: This section describes the simplest way to set up EasyShapes using Pixi.

docs.title: Installing Pixi
docs.text: • Install Pixi by following the instructions on the official Pixi Installation Guide.

docs.title: Setting up EasyShapes with Pixi
docs.text:
• Check that your system is supported: Windows (64-bit), Linux (x86-64, glibc 2.35 or newer, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+), or macOS 14 or newer on Apple Silicon.
  • Make sure Git is installed.

  • Choose a project location (local drive recommended).

    Windows + OneDrive

    We do not recommend creating a Pixi project inside OneDrive or other synced folders.

    By default, Pixi creates the virtual environment inside the project directory (in .pixi/). On Windows, synced folders such as OneDrive may cause file‑system issues (e.g., path-length limitations or restricted link operations), which can lead to unexpected install errors or environments being recreated.

    Instead, create your project in a local directory on your drive where you have full write permissions.

  • Download EasyShapes and navigate into it. Until the first release, the application is on the develop branch: 
    git clone --branch develop https://github.com/easyscience/shapes-app.git
cd shapes-app
  • Install EasyShapes and everything it needs: 
    pixi install
    This sets up the full development environment, including the tools for tests and documentation. The packaged application will be lighter.

docs.title: Running EasyShapes
docs.text:
• Start the application inside the shapes-app directory: 
    pixi run easyshapes-py

docs.title: Updating EasyShapes
docs.text:
• Get the latest version and install what it needs: 
    git pull
pixi install
    Use pixi install, not pixi update: pixi update moves to newer package versions than EasyShapes was tested with.
  • To update Pixi itself to the latest version: 
    pixi self-update

docs.title: Uninstalling EasyShapes and Pixi
docs.text:
• To remove EasyShapes, delete the shapes-app directory. Its environment is inside it, in .pixi/.
  • By default, your projects and the Shapespyer settings are saved outside that directory: in %APPDATA%\SimNavi\Shapespyer\ on Windows, in ~/Library/Application Support/Shapespyer/ on macOS, and in ~/.local/share/Shapespyer/ (projects) and ~/.config/Shapespyer/ (settings) on Linux. Delete them only if you no longer need your projects.
  • To uninstall Pixi, follow the official Pixi Guide.

docs.title: GROMACS optional
docs.text:
EasyShapes builds structures on its own. To equilibrate them (Analysis › Equilibration), it runs GROMACS, which you install yourself.

  • Install GROMACS by following the GROMACS installation guide. On Linux and macOS, package managers offer it (for example apt, Homebrew or conda-forge). On Windows, GROMACS has to be built from source; running EasyShapes inside WSL (Linux on Windows) is simpler.
  • EasyShapes runs gmx from your PATH. The Engine item in the status bar shows the GROMACS version it found, or why it can't run it.
  • If your GROMACS program has another name or is not on PATH (for example gmx_mpi), set it in the Shapespyer config.yaml, in the settings folder listed under Uninstalling: 
    gmx_executable: /path/to/gmx

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text: To work on the EasyShapes code itself (tests, formatting, documentation), see the Contributing Guidelines.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
EasyShapes is a scientific software for generation of ordered molecular aggregates and pre-assembled composite structures to seed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations aimed at studying equilibration (relaxation) processes in soft matter and biomolecular systems.

EasyShapes is developed as a cross-platform desktop application based on Qt and QML.

docs.title: License
docs.text: EasyShapes application is released under the BSD 3-Clause License.

docs.text:
The latest version of the EasyShapes application is missing_links.

For a complete list of new features, bug fixes, and improvements, see the GitHub Releases page.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
If you use EasyShapes application in your work, please cite Shapespyer, which builds its structures. Its Digital Object Identifier (DOI), for all versions, is 10.5281/zenodo.19074587.

Citation details in various styles (e.g., APA, MLA) and formats (e.g., BibTeX, JSON) are available on that Zenodo page.

The EasyShapes application will get its own DOI on Zenodo with its first release.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
We welcome contributions of any kind!

EasyShapes is intended to be a community-driven, open-source project supported by a diverse group of contributors.

The project is maintained by the European Spallation Source (ESS).

If you would like to report a bug or request a new feature, please use the GitHub Issue Tracker (A free GitHub account is required.)

To contribute code, documentation, or tests, please see our Contributing Guidelines for detailed development instructions.

docs.title: Questions and Feedback
docs.text: Ask questions or share feedback in GitHub Discussions, the discussion forum for the whole EasyShapes project. To report a bug, use the GitHub Issue Tracker.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: EasyShapes builds ordered molecular aggregates, such as vesicles, bilayers and micelles, as starting structures for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It can then equilibrate them with GROMACS and calculate their small-angle neutron scattering (SANS).

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The tabs at the top of the window lead through the work, from left to right:

  1. Home – click Start to open the Project page.
  2. Project – create a new project, open an existing one, or start from an example or a recent project.
  3. Sample Model – choose the structure type, add the components (molecules) and their fractions, set the structure's layers or lamellae and the buffer, then click Assemble. Continue opens the Analysis page.
  4. Analysis – equilibrate the structure with GROMACS (Equilibrate) and calculate its scattering curves (Calculate). Continue opens the Summary page.
  5. Summary – read an outline of the project and its results.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Each tutorial starts from a goal: the system to build and the result to aim for. Then it goes through only the controls needed to get there.

  • Multilamellar vesicle – build a vesicle of concentric lipid lamellae. No GROMACS needed.
  • SDS ball (micelle) – build a ball of SDS molecules, equilibrate it with GROMACS and calculate its scattering curve, following the Shapespyer example.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
One page per tab, describing each group and control:

  • Project
  • Sample Model
  • Analysis
  • Summary
